chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the sick person, and he said: 'He should prostrate on the ground, or on the hand-fan, or on a siwak (tooth-stick), raising it [higher than the ground], for that is superior to gesturing (with the head). Those who disliked prostrating on the hand-fan did so because of the idols that were worshipped besides Allah, but we have never worshipped anything other than Allah. So, let him prostrate on the hand-fan, or on a stick, or on a siwak.'

key_terms.اَلْإِيمَاء: Gesturing (typically with the head or eyes) to indicate prostration
key_terms.اَلْمِرْوَحَة: Hand-fan (a portable fan used in hot climates)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper method of prostration for a sick person who cannot stand in prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a sick person capable of prostration should do so physically on the ground, a hand-fan (mirwaha), or a siwak, rather than relying on head gestures (ima'), as physical prostration is superior. He clarifies that the historical aversion to prostrating on hand-fans stemmed from pre-Islamic idolaters worshipping the idols placed upon them, not from any inherent ritual impurity, thereby permitting its use for Muslims. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of distinguishing between cultural associations and intrinsic legal status in ritual acts.
